sentences.text:
Jani Begum vs Penta Lalitha on 11 November, 2024
 Hon'Ble Smt.Justice M.G.Priyadarsini
 M.A.C.M.A.No.2238 Of 2019
Judgment:

1. Dissatisfied with the compensation awarded by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal - cum - The Court of Chief Judge, City Civil Court, Hyderabad (hereinafter be referred as 'the Tribunal') in M.V.O.P.No.90 of 2014, dated 05.12.2017, the claim petitioners therein preferred the present Appeal seeking for enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: Court of Chief Judge, City Civil Court, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties hereinafter be referred as they were arrayed before the Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case are that the claim petitioners, who are the wife and children of the deceased-Mohd.Siddiq Khan filed a petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988against the respondents claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the death of the deceased in a motor vehicle accident that took place on 08.10.2013.

It is stated by the petitioners that on 08.10.2013, when the deceased was proceeding on his Auto bearing No.AP-11Y- 1988 towards Boggulakunta from Ramkoti X Road, in the meantime, one Swift car bearing No.AP-12M-9245 which was driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, dashed the Auto of the deceased due to which, he sustained grievous injuries all over the body and died on the spot.
Police of Sultanbazar Police MGP,J Station registered a case in Crime No.257 of 2013 under Section 304(A) IPC against the driver of the offending car.

It is stated by the petitioners that the deceased was aged 40 years and used to earn Rs.10,000/- per month by working as an Auto driver and used to contribute his earnings for maintenance of his family.

Due to the sudden death of the deceased,
the petitioners, who are dependents on the earnings of the deceased, lost their source of income and hence filed the claim petition claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- along with interest against the respondent Nos.1 & 2, who are the owner and insurer of the crime Swift car bearing No.AP-12M-9245.
4.
Though Respondent No.1, who is the owner of the crime vehicle, appeared through Advocate, but failed to file counter before the Trial Court.

Respondent No.2 filed his counter denying the averments made in the claim petition including, manner of accident, involvement of crime vehicle,
rash and negligent driving of the driver of the crime vehicle, age, occupation and income of the deceased and further contended that the driver of the crime vehicle do not possess valid and effective driving license and the vehicle was not road worthy to ply and hence, the Insurance Company is not liable to pay any compensation and that the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties and that the MGP,J claim made is excess and exorbitant and hence, prayed to dismiss the same.

5. Based on the above pleadings made by both the parties, the learned Tribunal had framed the following issues for trial:-

sentences.text:
Whether the pleaded accident had occurred resulting in death of deceased,
Mohd.Siddiq Khan to the rash and negligent driving of Maruthi Swift Car bearing No.AP-12M-9254 by its driver?

2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to any compensation and if so, at what quantum and what is the liability of the respondents?
3.
To what relief?
6. Before the Tribunal, on behalf of the petitioners, petitioner No.1, wife of the deceased, was examined as PW1 and got marked Exs.A1 to A8 through her.
As she is not an eye witness to the accident, she got examined PW2, who is an eye witness to the incident.
On behalf of respondents, no oral evidence was adduced, however Ex.B1- Copy of insurance policy was marked.

7. The learned Tribunal, after considering the evidence and documents available on record, had partly-allowed the claim petition of the petitioners by awarding compensation of Rs.10,05,000/-
along with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization payable by Respondent Nos.1& 2 jointly and severally.
Being not satisfied with the compensation MGP,J awarded by the Tribunal, the claim petitioners preferred the present Appeal seeking for enhancement of the same.
8. Heard learned counsel for the appellants as well as the learned Standing counsel for Respondent No.2/Insurance Company.
Perused the record.

9. The main contention of the learned counsel for Appellants is that the learned Tribunal erred in considering the income of the deceased @ Rs.5,000/-, which is on lower side and also erred in granting less compensation towards loss of consortium, loss of estate, loss of amenities of life,
funeral expenses, transportation charges and etc. and also awarded meager interest and therefore requested to allow the appeal by enhancing the compensation.

10. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondents contended that the learned Tribunal,
after considering the evidence and documents available on record, awarded reasonable compensation for which interference of this Court is unwarranted.
11. Now the point that arise for determination is, Whether the order passed by the learned Tribunal requires interference of this Court?

POINT:
12. This Court has perused the entire evidence and documents available on record.

As seen from the evidence of PWs 1 & 2 and documents marked under Ex.A1 to A6, it is evident that accident MGP,J had occurred on 08.10.2013 which resulted into the death of the deceased and the findings have attained finality since no appeal has been filed by the respondents.

A perusal of Ex.A1 shows that Police of Sultanbazar Police Station registered a case in Crime No.257 of 2013, under Section 304(A)
Jani Begum vs Penta Lalitha on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197090946/
2 IPC and filed charge sheet under Ex.A2 against the driver of the offending car.

sentences.text: Ex . A3
is the inquest report.
Ex . A4
is the post-mortem examination report.
Ex . A5
is the Motor Vehicle Inspector report.
Ex.A6 is the Panchanama of scene of offence.
Ex . A7
is the Aadhar card of deceased.
Ex.A8 is the Aadhar card of wife of deceased.
A perusal of Ex.B1-Insurance policy discloses that the policy was in existence as on the date of accident.
Hence, the only point that has to be decided by this Court in the present Appeal is whether the appellants/claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation.

13. Learned counsel for the appellants contended that though the deceased used to earn Rs.10,000/-
per month by working as an Auto-driver, but the learned Tribunal considered the income of the deceased @ Rs.5,000/- only which is very meagre.

In this regard, it is pertinent to mention that though the petitioners stated that the deceased is an Auto-driver, there is no documentary proof,
i.e., Driving license of the deceased, filed by the petitioners showing that the deceased used to earn Rs.10,000/- per month.

Hence, the MGP,J learned Tribunal, considering the age, and by following the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590 of 2014, took the income of the deceased @ Rs.5,000/- per month.

However, this Court, after giving due consideration to the year of accident, which happened in the year 2013, and considering the cost of living during the said period, finds it reasonable to fix the monthly income of the deceased @
Rs.6,000/- by interfering with the finding of the learned Tribunal.
14. It is pertinent to make a mention that the learned Tribunal, taking into consideration the age of the deceased as 40 years, awarded 40% towards future prospects.
But, as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case between National Insurance Co.Ltd. v.Pranay Sethi 1 40% should be added when the age of the deceased is less than 40 years.
In the instant case, the deceased is exactly 40 years old and is self-employed.
Hence, 25% should be added towards his future prospects instead of 40% and after addition of 25% towards his future prospects, then the income of the deceased comes to Rs.7,500/-.
As the number of dependents are 4, if 1/4this deducted towards his living and personal expenses, then the net monthly income comes to Rs.5,625/- and the annual income comes to Rs.67,500/-.
After applying the multiplier '15' as the deceased being aged 40 years, then the total loss of 2017(6) 170 SC MGP,J dependency would arrive at Rs.10,12,500/-.

Apart from this, the learned Tribunal had awarded an amount of Rs.10,000/- towards loss of love and affection,
Rs.30,000/- towards loss of consortium, Rs.10,000/- towards transportation and Rs.10,000/- for funeral expenses which this Court finds it to be meagre and is inclined to interfere with the same by awarding an amount of Rs.77,000/- towards conventional heads i.e. loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expensesby relying upon the Judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs.Pranay Sethi & others (2017 ACJ 2700).Apart from this

Hence, the total compensation to which the appellants are entitled to is arrived as under:-

Thus in all, the appellants are entitled for a total compensation of Rs.11,49,500/-.

15. Insofar as the interest is concerned,this Court by relying upon the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajesh and others v. Rajbir Singh and others 2enhances the rate of interest awarded by the Tribunal from 6% per annum to 7.5% per annum.

sentences.text: 16. In the result, the Appeal is partly-allowedby enhancing the compensation awarded by the learned Tribunal from Rs.10,05,000/- to Rs.11,49,500/-which shall carry interest @ 7.5% per annum payable by both the respondent Nos.1 & 2 jointly and severally within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
Upon such deposit, the appellants are entitled to 2 2013 ACJ 1403 = 2013 (4) ALT 35 MGP,J withdraw the same as per the apportionment made by the learned Tribunal.

However, a perusal of the proceeding sheet discloses that this Court vide orders dated 13.09.2019 passed in I.A.No.1 of 2019, condoned the delay caused in filing the Appeal subject to the condition that the computation of interest for the said delay period shall not be made.

As the Appeal is partly-allowed by enhancing the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal, hence the orders passed in I.A.No.1 of 2019 shall be given effect while calculating the interest component.
There shall be no order as to costs.
